leadBasedPaint.summary: For most housing built before 1978, sellers and landlords must disclose known lead-based paint and hazards, provide available records and the EPA pamphlet 'Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home', include the exact federal Lead Warning Statement, and get signed acknowledgments before the buyer or tenant is obligated. Buyers get a 10-day inspection opportunity unless waived. Keep records 3 years. Exemptions include 0-bedroom units, leases of 100 days or less, elderly or disabled housing without children under 6, foreclosure sales and certified lead-free housing.

sources.title: 40 CFR 745.113: certification and acknowledgment of disclosure (eCFR)
EPA: Real estate disclosures about potential lead hazards
EPA: Protect Your Family From Lead in Your Home (pamphlet)
42 U.S.C. §4852d: disclosure of information concerning lead upon transfer of residential property (Cornell LII)

dueOnSale.summary: The Garn-St Germain Act lets lenders enforce due-on-sale clauses, with exemptions for residential property of fewer than five units. Exemptions include transfers to a spouse or children, on death of a borrower to a relative, by divorce decree, into an inter vivos trust where the borrower remains a beneficiary and occupancy does not transfer, and leases of three years or less without an option to purchase. Sales subject-to, wraps, contracts for deed and lease-options to unrelated buyers are generally not exempt.

sources.title: Garn-St Germain Act due-on-sale provisions, 12 U.S.C. §1701j-3 (Cornell LII)

sellerFinancing.summary: Under Regulation Z, a person who regularly extends consumer credit secured by a dwelling can be a creditor and loan originator subject to ability-to-repay and loan-originator rules. Two seller-financer exclusions from the loan-originator definition: (1) a natural person, estate or trust financing one property in 12 months that it owns, did not build as a contractor, with no negative amortization and a fixed rate or adjustable after 5+ years; (2) any person financing three or fewer properties in 12 months that it owns, did not build, fully amortizing, with a good-faith ability-to-repay determination and a fixed or 5+-year adjustable rate. State SAFE Act laws may separately require a mortgage loan originator license.

sources.title: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.36 (loan originator rules, seller-financer exclusions) (eCFR)
Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.43 (ability-to-repay) (eCFR)
SAFE Act state licensing rules, 12 CFR Part 1008 (eCFR)

eSign.summary: The federal E-SIGN Act and state UETA laws (adopted by 49 states and DC; New York uses its own ESRA) make electronic signatures and records legally effective for most contracts. E-SIGN does not apply to wills and testamentary trusts, family-law matters, most UCC articles other than Articles 2 and 2A (so UCC Article 3 negotiable instruments are excluded), court documents, and notices of utility shutoff, default, foreclosure, eviction or right to cure for a primary residence, among others. Recording and notarization follow state law.

sources.title: Electronic Signatures in Global and National Commerce Act, 15 U.S.C. §7001 (Cornell LII)
E-SIGN exceptions, 15 U.S.C. §7003 (Cornell LII)

firpta.summary: When the seller is a foreign person, the buyer generally must withhold 15% of the amount realized and remit it to the IRS, unless an exception applies. Get a certification of non-foreign status or other FIRPTA documentation at closing.

sources.title: IRS: FIRPTA withholding

fairHousingRoomRentals.summary: The Fair Housing Act exempts some owner-occupied dwellings with four or fewer units from some provisions, but not from the ban on discriminatory advertising. The Ninth Circuit held the Act does not reach roommate selection within a single shared dwelling (Fair Housing Council v. Roommate.com, 2012). State and local laws may be broader.
